The offering is contingent on Digital Realty's acquisition of Blackstone's interests in two Northern Virginia data center joint ventures (Digital Carver Dulles 9 and Digital Carver Brickyard), expected to close on June 30, 2026. Digital Realty will not receive proceeds from the secondary offering.

META.title: A Former CIA Advisor Says This Tech Boom Is Already Bigger Than the Internet Ever Was
META.summary: Financial researcher Jim Rickards warns that the $5 trillion AI data center buildout in the U.S. may mirror the dot-com bubble, with companies creating circular revenue streams through chip and cloud capacity sales. Unlike the internet boom, AI faces physical and energy constraints, with experts suggesting diminishing returns on compute investments. Rickards highlights July 29th Meta earnings as a potential turning point, comparing it to March 2000 when a Barron's article triggered the Nasdaq's 80% decline.

META.title: AI Companies Are Spending Billions Before They Even Make a Dime
META.summary: Major AI companies are spending over $1 billion monthly while losing money, with nearly $5 trillion projected for U.S. data center investments despite 95% of corporate AI initiatives failing to deliver measurable ROI. Financial analyst Jim Rickards warns that investor expectations may be outpacing reality, and upcoming earnings reports—particularly Meta's July 29th forecast—could reveal whether spending aligns with business results. The AI boom's financing through complex debt structures similar to pre-2008 mortgage bundling poses systemic risks to pension funds and broader markets.

NTNX.title: Nutanix and the North Carolina School of Science and Mathematics Partner to Expand Computer Science Access Across North Carolina

The floating-rate loan features a 36-month initial term and is projected to deliver over $1 million in annual interest savings, demonstrating the firm's disciplined debt management capabilities.

EOSE.title: Eos Announces $125 Million Investment for Frontier Power USA, Bringing Expected Frontier Equity Investment up to $375 Million
EOSE.summary: Eos Energy Enterprises announced a $125 million investment from Hudson Bay Capital Management to support its investment in Frontier Power USA (FPUSA), bringing the platform's expected equity base to approximately $375 million. This capital is structured to support over $1.5 billion in project deployment. The funding includes Hudson Bay's $75 million equity investment in Eos and $50 million direct investment in FPUSA, complementing previous commitments from Cerberus Capital Management ($100 million) and Eos' own contribution (up to $150 million through a rights offering). FPUSA has a robust pipeline of approximately 16 GWh of long-duration energy storage projects.

The rights offering is scheduled to commence on July 2, 2026, with completion subject to certain conditions.

EOSE.title: Eos Announces Pricing of Registered Direct Offering of Common Stock and Warrants to Fund Investment in Frontier Power USA
EOSE.summary: Eos Energy Enterprises announced a registered direct offering of 13.7 million shares and 6 million warrants to Hudson Bay Capital Management for approximately $75 million. Combined with Hudson Bay's $50 million direct investment in Frontier Power USA (FPUSA), the expected equity investment reaches $375 million. FPUSA plans to deploy over $1.5 billion in project capital with a 16 GWh pipeline of long-duration energy storage projects across U.S. markets.

AVPT.title: AvePoint Research Reveals AI Visibility Gaps Have Nearly Tripled as AI Agents Scale and Almost Half of Enterprise Employees Now Rely on Agents Daily or Weekly
AVPT.summary: AvePoint's third annual State of AI Report reveals critical governance gaps in enterprise AI adoption. Visibility gaps for unsanctioned AI tools have nearly tripled to 17.6%, while 21.1% of organizations lack visibility into AI agent usage.
